slot.brief: Standard cell EMF: add two given half-cell reduction potentials with appropriate reversal, compute E°cell; straightforward single-formula number.

verdicts.working: For Zn|Zn²⁺||Ag⁺|Ag, Ag is the cathode and Zn is the anode. E°cell = 0.80 − (−0.76) = 1.56 V.

working:
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=E^\circ_{\text{cathode}}-E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$
$=0.80-(-0.76)=1.56\ \text{V}$

Independent check: For Zn|Zn²⁺||Ag⁺|Ag, Ag is the cathode and Zn is the anode. E°cell = 0.80 − (−0.76) = 1.56 V.
solution:
For a galvanic cell, $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=E^\circ_{\text{cathode}}-E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$. Here, Ag is the cathode and Zn is the anode:
$$E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=0.80-(-0.76)=1.56\ \text{V}$$

draft.distractor_notes: A: reverses the cell reaction. B: adds the reduction potentials without reversing the anode reaction. C: reports only the magnitude of the zinc potential.
